doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: Listening to radio bands with his father
summary: His father pointed him to the bands on the radio, from Ellington to Whiteman and Guy Lombardo, and taught him to appreciate every style.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Do you recall if your parents listened to the music that you liked and how did they feel about it? Did they feel that —

My father, being a musician, is the one that pointed me I guess in the right direction, and my mother too for that matter. But my father used to listen, we had the radio and that’s all you had, and you listened to the old bands, some of which people wonder where I’m coming from with this, but there were bands like Gus Anheim, Paul Whiteman of course and Duke Ellington was one of my father’s favorites, and there was Cab Calloway and Fletcher Henderson and all these different bands, and then we used to listen to Horace Heidt and those bands, and we listened to every band because they were playing all the time. Any time you turned on the radio, day or night, you could hear some of these orchestras. My father listened to them intently. And so I came up listening to all these things, and without having someone point it out to me I just acquired an appreciation for all the different styles that I heard. And my father was even a fan of the [scats] Wayne King and Guy Lombardo.
Yeah. He even liked the syrupy stuff.
He liked all these and so through him I learned to appreciate all of these bands. You could identify them because their styles were so different.
